leagues.name: FIA World Endurance Championship
notes: 20 teams run the 35 full-season 2026 entries per the official fiawec.com grid page (fetched 2026-09-26): 10 Hypercar teams and 10 LMGT3 teams; the target brief's 35 counts cars (17 Hypercar, 18 LMGT3) from 14 manufacturers.

Hypercar entries: Alpine Endurance Team (#35/#36), Aston Martin THOR Team (#007/#009), BMW M Team WRT (#15/#20), Cadillac Hertz Team JOTA (#12/#38), Ferrari AF Corse (#50/#51), AF Corse (#83), Genesis Magma Racing (#17/#19), Peugeot TotalEnergies (#93/#94), Toyota Racing (#7/#8) - 17 cars. LMGT3: Heart of Racing (#23/#27), Team WRT (#32/#69), TF Sport (#33), Racing Team Turkey by TF (#34), Vista AF Corse (#21/#54), Proton Competition (#77/#88), Akkodis ASP (#78/#87), Garage 59 (#10/#58), Iron Lynx (#61/#79), Manthey (DK Engineering #91, The Bend #92) - 18 cars.

2026 calendar (8 rounds): Prologue Imola 14 Apr; Imola 19 Apr; TotalEnergies 6 Hours of Spa-Francorchamps 9 May; 24 Hours of Le Mans 13-14 Jun; Rolex 6 Hours of Sao Paulo 12 Jul; Lone Star Le Mans (COTA) 6 Sep; 6 Hours of Fuji 27 Sep; 6 Hours of Barcelona 18 Oct; 6 Hours of Monza 8 Nov (fiawec.com homepage and entry-list news, fetched 2026-09-25/26).

Both 2026 Gulf rounds were lost to the Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz shipping risk: the Qatar 1812km was postponed from March (fiawec.com statement 1 Mar and rescheduling 13 Mar 2026) and then cancelled with Bahrain's finale, both replaced by Barcelona and Monza (Motorsport.com, 2026-07-28).

Both Gulf rounds return in 2027: Prologue Lusail 21-22 Mar, Qatar 1812km 25-27 Mar, and Bapco Energies 8 Hours of Bahrain 4-6 Nov, in a nine-round calendar that also restores Silverstone (fiawec.com 2027-calendar news, fetched 2026-09-26).

Series partners per the fiawec.com partners page (fetched 2026-09-26): Rolex, TotalEnergies, Michelin, DHL, Goodyear, CrowdStrike, Motul, Bosch; suppliers Pommery, Al Kamel, MRTC, AMP Visual TV. Goodyear is the exclusive LMGT3 tyre supplier to at least 2029 (fiawec.com news, 2026-06-11).

Car-livery placements do not fit the schema yet; car-level sponsor facts are recorded in unsourced. Team title sponsors carried in team names are entered as kits with a front placement mapped from 'team title/name', mirroring the motogp research.

claims.text: Bapco Energies is Bahrain's national integrated oil and gas company and titles the WEC season finale, while Human Rights Watch reports that in 2026 Bahraini authorities arbitrarily arrested dozens of people, that Mohammed Almosawi died in custody with signs of torture after being forcibly disappeared, and that 67 people had their citizenship stripped.
claims.short: Bahrain state energy company titles the WEC finale; HRW documents 2026 arrests, a death in custody, citizenship-stripping

claims.short: Qatar state bodies host the WEC season opener; Amnesty documents migrant-worker exploitation and restricted expression

proposedRatings.reasoning: Bahrain's national oil company titles the season finale and hosts it at the state-owned Bahrain International Circuit (10-year extension announced 12 Jun 2026). State money: HRW's 2026 Bahrain record (arbitrary arrests, torture-signed death in custody, citizenship-stripping, detained rights defenders) puts a Kingdom's flagship energy brand at serious, matching the DP World Tour treatment of the same company and Bahrain's 'Victorious Bahrain' sportswashing brand.

Already rated serious in the corpus: Qatar Airways Group is wholly owned by the Qatari state. Its 2024 WEC deal made it title partner of the Qatar 1812km and trackside branding at Lusail; the same Gulf-state record (migrant-worker abuse, restricted expression) carries over. Serious rather than severe: Qatar is not party to an armed conflict.

unsourced: Car-livery sponsors on the 35 full-season cars: the car-livery shape does not fit the schema yet. Official car pages (fiawec.com/en/car/2026/<num>, fetched 2026-09-26) show manufacturer and tyre partner (Michelin for all 10 Hypercar teams; Goodyear for LMGT3) but no car-level sponsor list; per-car livery sponsors must be collected from team launches.

Manufacturer ownership links (indirect, not sponsorship): PIF holds 19.5% of Aston Martin Lagonda, whose Valkyrie Hypercars are run by the Aston Martin THOR Team (CarExpert, 2025-11-19); CYVN Holdings (Abu Dhabi) completed the acquisition of McLaren Automotive and a non-controlling McLaren Racing stake in April 2025, and McLaren runs Garage 59's LMGT3 programme (McLaren Racing, 2025-04-03); Bahrain's Mumtalakat remains McLaren Racing's major shareholder (McLaren Racing, 2025-04-03). CYVN's own ownership by the Abu Dhabi government is not stated in the announcement and was not verified.

2026 race titles with state links: the 2026 edition of the season opener was to be the plain 'Qatar 1812km' at Lusail (postponed 13 Mar 2026 with the Prologue, then cancelled outright with the Bahrain finale on 28 Jul 2026, replaced by Barcelona 18 Oct and Monza 8 Nov - Motorsport.com, Rachit Thukral, 2026-07-28); the finale was to be the Bapco Energies 8 Hours of Bahrain (2026 entry-list news, 2025-12-08). The event-host shape does not fit the schema yet.

Bahrain host-contract fact: Bahrain International Circuit's agreement with FIA WEC was extended so the circuit hosts the series 'until at least 2036' (fiawec.com news 'Bahrain to host FIA WEC for next ten years', 2026-06-12). BIC is a Bahraini state-linked venue (its chief executive is a member of the ruling family), but the announcement itself does not state BIC's ownership, so no owner link was recorded.

2027 Gulf returns: Prologue at Lusail 21-22 Mar and Qatar 1812km 25-27 Mar 2027; Bapco Energies 8 Hours of Bahrain 4-6 Nov 2027 (fiawec.com 2027-calendar news, published 2026-06-12, fetched 2026-09-26). No title sponsor is shown for the 2027 Qatar race; the race is hosted at Lusail by the Qatari state-linked circuit and QMMF.

Qatar Airways' WEC role beyond 2024: Qatar Airways was named Official Title Partner and Airline Partner of the 'Qatar Airways Qatar 1812 Km' with trackside branding (fiawec.com news, 2024-02-15). Whether the deal was renewed after the 2026 cancellation is not known; the 2027 race name carries no title sponsor on the official calendar.

Peugeot's Hypercar team competes as 'Peugeot TotalEnergies' per the official grid page, so TotalEnergies is the team title sponsor; a primary source naming the deal terms was not collected. Similarly 'Cadillac Hertz Team JOTA' carries Hertz as title sponsor of the JOTA-run Cadillacs (livery unveiled 13 Jan 2025, fiawec.com); Hertz's ownership was not researched. 'BMW M Team WRT', 'Akkodis ASP Team', 'Genesis Magma Racing', 'Aston Martin THOR Team' and 'Vista AF Corse' similarly carry names of sponsors/owners not individually sourced here.

The 2026 entry-list PDF (https://www.fiawec.com/umbrella_media/wec26-entrylist-a4-6936d72065269710536636.pdf) was not opened (PDF); per-car sponsors and driver/nationality detail come from the fiawec.com grid and car pages instead.
WEC suppliers (fiawec.com 'Our Suppliers' page, fetched 2026-09-26): Pommery, Al Kamel (timing), MRTC, AMP Visual TV - supplier relationships, not carried into the schema.

Motul ownership: Motul is part of Integra Eco/Integra Eco Industries group per its own site (not fetched here); Bosch GmbH is majority-held by the Robert Bosch Stiftung charitable foundation per general knowledge - neither chain verified from a primary source during this research.
